newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical giants on track for strong year.
newsitem.headline: German chemical giants on track for strong year.

text.p: Germany's largest chemical groups appear poised to deliver strong full-year results despite presenting a mixed picture for the first nine months with improved currency relations offset by softer prices.

Compared with leading European industry powerhouses, analysts agreed the three German giants, Bayer AG, Hoechst AG and BASF AG were quality players, promising a fairly strong performance amid difficult conditions.
"Overall the outlook is not that negative and (Germany's three big chemical groups) should all post stronger results for the full year," said BHF Bank analyst Ronald Koehler.

The three groups announced nine-month and third quarter results over the last two weeks and all benefited from a weaker mark, which makes German exports cheaper abroad. But all three maintained that lower prices were weighing heavy on results.
The three companies also benefited from acquisitions and divestments, a particularly strong trend at Hoechst.

Analysts said BASF, while generally extremely conservative in its outlook, appeared to be faring the best of the three at the moment, having successfully realigned its portfolio making it less susceptible to cyclical swings.

BASF distinguished itself from rivals with stronger third quarter growth and comments that prices were picking up again in certain segments and that business conditions would continue to be livelier in coming months.

"The highlight at BASF is the big investment in oil and gas operations which is now paying off," said Peter Houghton, analyst at JP Morgan in London. Oil and gas sales jumped 12.4 percent to 3.5 billion marks ($2.32 billion) and were a key engine for growth.
In addition, BASF, previously lagging behind rivals in health care, invested in the sector with the acquisition of the drugs business from U.K.'s Boots generating half of all sales.
Analysts also expect BASF will soon be eyeing new takeover targets as chief executive Juergen Strube said BASF intended to participate in the general industry consolidation.
But the undisputed leader in the health care area is still Bayer AG, according to analysts who said it was benefiting from a "drugs bonus" after previewing several promising new drugs.
On the other hand, Bayer underscored the unsatisfactory price situation more vividly and chief executive Manfred Schneider said Bayer was not wholly satisfied with results.
Foreign sales generally far outpaced domestic sales at Hoechst and Bayer, with only BASF reporting relatively strong German growth. Again this is related to oil and gas sales.
BHF's Koehler said Bayer may feel the pressure of costly introductions of the new drugs as their launch dates approach.

Hoechst, receiving top marks from analysts for promoting the concept of shareholder value, also presented a very mixed picture. "The underlying numbers were disappointing," said Tony Cox, analyst at Kleinwort Benson in London after Hoechst's chairman Juergen Dormann called the operating business "poor".
Propping up Hoechst's results however are high extraordinary earnings brought in by the sale of its SGL Carbon and Uhde units. This should help the full year picture as well.
Encouraging for the longer term are Hoechst's plans to transform the company into a strategic management holding group keeping its hands out of the operating business, analysts said.

While several analysts worried that Hoechst's promised lower costs, related to massive restructurings, were not filtering through to results yet, JP Morgan's Houghton noted "Hoechst has delivered on health care where the margins are moving up."

Analysts agree soft prices will continue to plague Hoechst far more than the others as prices for PET remain quite weak. Bayer too could face some trouble as it supplies the construction industry which shows no signs of recovering.
Nonetheless, analysts predict each of the companies will present full year results outpacing last year's record sales and profit figures and will all pay a higher dividend.
